narratives.Overview:
## Summary

scope:provenance rejects canonical scope:complete evidence as intent drift

## Context

Directive v0.109.1 in consumer bxc-3ci/FreshserviceAI. Issue #372 was implemented and merged in PR #376 at 2890691ce96ea5e3e650cc6806b6e5c7f194b917, with required hosted validate and all declared local checks green. Its active human-approved xBRIEF has non-empty file_scope and five non-terminal plan.items. Adding schema-valid plan.items[].x-directive/evidence records for post-merge completion makes the real verify:scope-provenance probe fail.

## Expected behavior

The exact canonical x-directive/evidence field required by scope:complete should be treated as guarded completion metadata on an existing approved item identity, not as a change to approved product intent. Provenance must continue to reject changed item identity, title, narrative, acceptance meaning, file_scope, new or removed items, arbitrary unknown keys, and invalid or unauthorized dispositions.

## Actual behavior / gap

scope:complete requires plan.items[].x-directive/evidence, but verify:scope-provenance does not classify that field as machine/completion metadata. It includes the field in extracted item intent and records it as unknown. The consumer probe exits 1 with both intent-drift (extracted items changed) and unclassified-key (items[].x-directive/evidence absent from the approved base preimage), requiring a fresh human remint even though neither product intent nor file_scope changed.

## Session notes

## Minimal reproduction

1. Create and human-approve an active xBRIEF with non-empty `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope` and at least one non-terminal `plan.items` entry.
2. Keep item identity, narrative, acceptance meaning, and file scope unchanged.
3. Add a schema-valid `plan.items[].x-directive/evidence` object containing `kind`, `pointer`, `recorded_at`, and `recorded_by`, as required by `scope:complete`.
4. Run:

   ```bash
   deft verify:scope-provenance \
     --project-root . \
     --base-ref origin/main \
     --enforce
   ```

5. Observe both `intent-drift` for the item array and `unclassified-key` for `items[].x-directive/evidence`.

The FreshserviceAI #372 closeout reproduced this with five evidence-bearing items after its product change and required CI had merged. No lifecycle move occurred.

## Root cause evidence in v0.109.1

- [`scope/acceptance-evidence.ts:29-33`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.109.1/packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts#L29-L33) defines the literal canonical keys, and [`:391-470`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.109.1/packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts#L391-L470) requires evidence or a valid human-origin disposition for every non-terminal criterion.
- [`scope-provenance/known-machine.ts:54-70`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.109.1/packages/core/src/scope-provenance/known-machine.ts#L54-L70) omits `x-directive/evidence` from `ITEM_MACHINE_KEYS`.
- [`scope-provenance/extract-intent.ts:122-164`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.109.1/packages/core/src/scope-provenance/extract-intent.ts#L122-L164) therefore copies the field into extracted item intent and records its path as unknown.
- [`scope-provenance/compare-intent.ts:98-109`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.109.1/packages/core/src/scope-provenance/compare-intent.ts#L98-L109) reports item drift, while [`:234-262`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.109.1/packages/core/src/scope-provenance/compare-intent.ts#L234-L262) emits `unclassified-key`.

This is a missed cross-gate regression between two previously delivered contracts:

- [#3305](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3305) standardized the namespaced evidence/disposition keys so completion evidence could coexist with conformance.
- [#3385](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3385) introduced extracted-intent preimage authority and the known-machine/unknown-key split.

Each feature is internally consistent, but their combined production path was not covered: the canonical completion field introduced by #3305 was not classified for the provenance model introduced by #3385.

## Proposed fix

Treat only the exact canonical `x-directive/evidence` field on an already-approved item or nested-item identity as post-approval completion metadata.

- Exclude that exact field from intent comparison, or otherwise suppress only its matching unknown-path finding.
- Continue validating its schema and semantic suitability through the acceptance-evidence gate.
- Preserve comparison of item IDs, titles, narratives, summaries, types, acceptance meaning, and every other extracted field.
- Continue rejecting new or removed items and arbitrary unknown keys.
- Do not broadly exempt the `x-directive/` namespace.
- Do not weaken the human-origin safeguards for `x-directive/disposition`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Adding schema-valid `x-directive/evidence` to an existing approved item does not produce `intent-drift` or `unclassified-key`.
- [ ] The same regression covers nested items/sub-items.
- [ ] Changing item identity, title, narrative, acceptance meaning, file scope, or an arbitrary unknown key still fails provenance.
- [ ] Adding or removing an item still fails provenance.
- [ ] Malformed or unsuitable evidence still fails the acceptance-evidence gate.
- [ ] `x-directive/disposition` retains its human-origin safeguards.
- [ ] An end-to-end `runTransition("complete")` fixture proves canonical evidence passes provenance and the evidence gate together.
- [ ] The normal aggregate quality gate exercises this cross-gate fixture.
- [ ] No broad namespace exemption or production skip flag is introduced.

## Workarounds evaluated

- Same-change remint is correctly rejected as self-authorization.
- An agent-authored human approval is prohibited by the human-presence gate.
- Fabricating or editing approval artifacts, pre-marking items complete, manually moving the brief, or using the internal test-only skip would bypass required gates.
- A genuine human review plus approval-only precursor can remint the exact evidence-bearing preimage, but it turns routine completion metadata into a new intent-approval cycle and does not address the bank replay defect reported separately.

Consumer reproduction: [bxc-3ci/FreshserviceAI#372](https://github.com/bxc-3ci/FreshserviceAI/issues/372), delivered by [PR #376](https://github.com/bxc-3ci/FreshserviceAI/pull/376).

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-01T21:25:10Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

Re-verified at SHA f96963e9ce2a9bab41fdc2646e67380e8bf0dbaa. Ceiling comment 5500539162.

## Verdict

The refutation-target holds for top-level `plan.items[]` identities that `extractItems` already walks: `ITEM_MACHINE_KEYS` / `classifyItemKey` is the existing omit path, so both `intent-drift` (`compareItems`) and `unclassified-key` stop firing, and that is the right inventory choice over a new skip flag or an `x-directive/` prefix. It does not hold as the whole remedy once nested item identities or the object shape of the evidence field are in scope.

## Nested extract walk (sharpens-framing)

Evidence. `ITEM_MACHINE_KEYS` in `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/known-machine.ts` classifies only immediate keys of each top-level item. `extractItems` in `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/extract-intent.ts` is a single-level loop: copy `ITEM_EXTRACT_KEYS`, then copy every non-machine leftover wholesale and record `items[].${key}`. It does not recurse. The complete-time evidence gate does recurse: `walkItems` in `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts` walks `subItems` and nested `items`, and `ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE_KEY` is required on those identities. `compareItems` in `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/compare-intent.ts` is a wholesale canonical compare of the extracted item array.

Failure mode. Schema-valid nested `x-directive/evidence` lives inside the unknown wholesale `items` / `subItems` copy. After adding the key to `ITEM_MACHINE_KEYS` only, a top-level consumer probe goes green; nested evidence still changes the extracted parent item and `compareItems` still emits `intent-drift`. `unclassified-key` often does not name the nested evidence path, because the recorded unknown path is `items[].items` or `items[].subItems`, already present on the minted preimage.

Disposition. Restate the remedy as classification of that exact key at every item identity the evidence gate already walks. Nested coverage cannot be a naive recursive `extractItems` that starts omitting nested `status` / `completed` / `effort`: those fields are hashed today inside the wholesale nested copy, and `known-machine.ts` forbids a classification growth that changes existing intent digests. Nested coverage, if kept, is an evidence-key omit through those nested arrays that leaves other nested fields as they are hashed today. If that restatement is refused, the nested acceptance criterion is out of this target.

## Object-valued machine omit (sharpens-framing)

Evidence. Every current `ITEM_MACHINE_KEYS` entry is a scalar (`status`, `completed`, `percentComplete`, `effort`, `updated`, `created`, `planRef`, `plan_ref`). `x-directive/evidence` is an object. Machine classification omits the whole key. `parseEvidence` in `acceptance-evidence.ts` requires `kind` / `pointer` / `recorded_at` / `recorded_by` and does not reject additional properties. `evaluateScopeProvenance` does not run the evidence gate; it only lists `xbrief/active/`.

Failure mode. After mint, an agent can add extra properties on the evidence object, or replace a valid pointer with another schema-valid pointer, without remint. Provenance cannot see the object. Complete still accepts extra properties. That is a new post-approval write channel: current item machine keys cannot carry a nested payload.

Disposition. Pair machine-omit with closing extra properties on that object in the existing evidence parser, or record expressly that extra properties on completion-evidence are ungoverned. Do not add a third provenance class.

Injection / swarm. This target widens what may change after human mint without remint. The intended grant is agent-stamped completion evidence (`x-directive/disposition` stays unknown and `parseDisposition` still uses `isHumanOrigin`). The unintended grant is an opaque object on every approved item. Closing extra properties uses `parseEvidence`; it does not require a new fence.

## Writer-discipline pair (footnote)

`KNOWN_MACHINE_WRITERS` is the documented same-PR annotation. `allKnownMachineLeaves()` enumerates writer keys, not `ITEM_MACHINE_KEYS`, so adding the field to the set without `plan.items[].x-directive/evidence` still typechecks. The stamp helper to name as writer is `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts`.

## Disposition key stays unknown (footnote)

`x-directive/disposition` is absent from `ITEM_MACHINE_KEYS`. Adding a waiver after mint still extracts as unknown and still remints. That matches the issue keep on human-origin safeguards.

## Unknown-path suppression is not a second remedy (footnote)

`compareUnknownKeys` records synthetic `items[].<key>` paths and does not walk the items array. Suppressing only that `unclassified-key` leaves the field in the extracted item, so `compareItems` still reports `intent-drift`. Classification (omit from extract) is the mechanism that kills both findings. The issue body's "or suppress only its matching unknown-path finding" alternative is not viable against this SHA.

## Inventory

Used, not invented: `ITEM_MACHINE_KEYS` + `classifyItemKey`; `ITEM_EXTRACT_KEYS`; unknown-path `unclassified-key`; wholesale `compareItems`; `KNOWN_MACHINE_WRITERS`; metadata analog `plan.metadata.completionProvenance`; `ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE_KEY` / `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` / `isHumanOrigin`; `walkItems` recursion; duplicate-key tokenizer; active-only provenance scan.

Not used: `x-directive/` prefix exemption; production skip flags; guarded-append on item fields; a new key class.

## Road not taken

Guarded absent-to-present for this field (allow first stamp, remint on later mutation) instead of machine omit.

Steelman. Machine omit also hides evidence mutation after the first stamp. Guarded-append would catch a later pointer swap. That would be stronger if pointer mutation without remint were in-scope as an authorization defect.

What would flip. A consumer of evidence other than the complete-time evidence gate, or a requirement that the minted preimage pin the first evidence object. Neither exists at this SHA: `status` / `completed` already mutate without remint, and complete re-reads the live object. Guarded-append would be a new item-field class. Rejected.

## Cross-gate fixture (footnote)

`runTransition("complete")` moves the brief out of `xbrief/active/`. `evaluateScopeProvenance` only lists active briefs. The consumer probe is evidence added while still active. A fixture that only checks provenance after complete does not exercise the failing gate.

## Bound remedy (reading of the takes)

1. Classify the exact canonical evidence key as item machine metadata at every item identity `walkItems` already walks (`plan.items[]`, nested `items`, `subItems`). That omit is the mechanism that kills both intent-drift and unclassified-key. Do not suppress only the unknown-path finding.

4. `x-directive/disposition` stays unknown. Writer annotation lands in the same PR as the new machine key. A provenance fixture must exercise the field while the brief is still active.

This lean does not auto-stamp by itself. Operator yolo on the dispatch turn is recorded as confirm of this all-accept map.
